Sources, historical conventions and unresolved links

The two branches meet at Rodolphe: his PhD advisor Dirk Aeyels on the left, and his postdoctoral mentor Petar Kokotović on the right. The postdoctoral link is documented in the preface to Constructive Nonlinear Control; older edges follow Mathematics Genealogy Project (MGP) records.

The mathematical branch reaches Euler through his correspondence with Lagrange. Laplace is a separate teacher of Poisson, not a descendant of Euler in this selected tree. Chasles and Poisson are shown with their historical schooling rather than modern-equivalent doctorate claims; Newton’s Yale B.A. date is not the date of his later study with Chasles.

The right branch passes through medical degree records at Tübingen, Basel and Padua. The medicine and physiology heading identifies the historical disciplinary root; the lineage also includes chemists, physicists, philosophers and astronomers.

From the Renaissance toward Avicenna, the chain records earlier teachers and intellectual associations. It is not a proven uninterrupted chain of doctoral supervision. The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy describes Khayyam’s study with Bahmanyār as possible, and this link is marked uncertain even in the compact view.

Mitscherlich’s link with Stromeyer is marked as recorded academic mentorship. Leoniceno’s link to Bonisoli belongs to earlier schooling, not to his medical doctorate. MGP also lists Tsypkin as a mentor of Kokotović; this selected route follows Feldbaum. Andronov was an opponent in Tsypkin’s record and is not shown as Tsypkin’s supervisor.

These are selected routes in a contributed database, checked in September 2026. Every displayed name links to its MGP record; older historical associations have not all been independently established from original manuscripts.
